Thought: I need to determine what aliphatic saturated hydrocarbons are also known as. Let me analyze each option.

Aliphatic hydrocarbons are compounds made up of carbon and hydrogen atoms arranged in straight chains, branched chains, or non-aromatic rings.

Saturated hydrocarbons have single bonds between carbon atoms (no double or triple bonds).

Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with single bonds only.
Alkenes have at least one carbon-carbon double bond, so they are unsaturated.
Alkynes have at least one carbon-carbon triple bond, so they are unsaturated.
Paraffins is another name for alkanes in the petroleum industry.

Looking at the options:
A. Alkanes and alkenes - Incorrect because alkenes are unsaturated
B. Alkanes and paraffins - Correct because both terms refer to saturated hydrocarbons
C. Alkenes and alkynes - Incorrect because both are unsaturated hydrocarbons
D. Paraffins and alkenes - Incorrect because alkenes are unsaturated
Final Answer: [ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
